We had a wonderful vacation at Rixos Premium Belek. We’ve stayed at several Rixos properties over the years, including Tekirova, Sungate, Bodrum, and Sharm El Sheikh, and in our opinion, Rixos Premium Belek offers the best food of them all. The variety, quality, and taste were outstanding throughout our stay.

The à la carte restaurants were excellent, especially the Turkish Restaurant and the Greek Restaurant. One tip: make sure you book your reservation right at 10:00 AM. We found that it’s much easier to disconnect from the hotel’s Wi-Fi and use your mobile data instead. Start refreshing the reservation page around 9:59 AM because the popular restaurants fill up within minutes.

If your priority is the food, we thought the Turkish Restaurant offered the best dining experience. If you’re looking for a lively evening with music, dancing, and entertainment, then the Greek Restaurant is the perfect choice.

The pools are beautiful, spacious, and perfect for families. As for the sea, it’s the typical Belek coastline. The water is clean, but because the seabed is sandy, it can appear a little cloudy. If you’re expecting the crystal-clear waters of Bodrum or Didim, this is different—but the sea itself is clean and enjoyable.

We were also pleasantly surprised to receive another room upgrade, which we truly appreciated. Thank you to the team for making us feel valued once again.

The only downside was that the resort can feel quite crowded during peak season. However, that’s understandable given the size and popularity of the property.

Overall, we had an excellent stay and would happily return. Rixos Premium Belek continues to be one of our favorite all-inclusive resorts.

I was truly surprised and disappointed by the lack of attention we experienced from the moment we checked into the hotel today.

We, a family of 14 including our children, booked 5 rooms for 5 nights at your hotel. During check-in, we were assigned a staff member named Serdar. He later said that another lady would contact us shortly to assist us. However, hours passed and no one contacted us.

Upon this, I called Serdar to remind him of the situation. I was told that they would contact me again. Despite this, there was still no response. When I called Serdar again, my calls went unanswered.

Frankly, I did not expect such a lack of attention at a prestigious hotel like Rixos. Especially with a large family booking of 5 rooms for 5 nights, I believe guests should receive the necessary attention.

At the very least, we would have expected a guest representative to introduce the facility, explain the restaurants, activities, children's programs, and services offered in detail, preferably someone who speaks Arabic. Unfortunately, we didn't experience any of that.

It wasn't just a lack of information; we felt like we weren't guests at all, but rather forgotten. It's truly upsetting to have had such an impression on the very first day of our holiday.

After two weeks at the Rixos Belek, I have very mixed feelings.

Unfortunately, the hotel wasn't worth the money, even though it's not a bad hotel.

We were bothered by the constant attempts to charge extra at every turn. Whether it was in the à la carte restaurants for "special" dishes, better seating, or loungers in the "Infinia" program (no idea what that's supposed to be). Upon arrival, we were called to reception with a fantastic offer: for just €6,000 more, we could upgrade to a suite... okay... what's the big deal? :-D

The hotel itself is clean and well-maintained, and the grounds are enormous. Enormous, but pointlessly so; there's a lack of space in the restaurants and pools. Instead, there are lots of lawns in places you'll hardly ever see. In the main restaurant, there's an 16+ section that's practically right next to the usual canteen madness, with open walls. It was impossible for me to eat inside because of the noise. There are only about 20 tables on the terrace for 1500 guests; that's simply impossible...

Vacation is always a socially unusual situation, and here in particular, there's the contact with some extremely wealthy people who arrive with nannies, talk about their McLaren collections, and there are also a lot of "influencers," women who have all been to the same surgeon, a great many Russians and Arabs of all kinds, some Turkish, and some Western European guests. About 80% are families with children. Unfortunately, there are also the usual alcoholics, plate hogs, and sunbed hogs.

The food is standard for an upscale Turkish vacation, as you would expect from other 5-star hotels. Nothing special, but not bad either. It's clear, as in every hotel in Turkey, that they skimp on meat because it's simply very expensive.

The drinks selection is also good, but nothing special.

The QR pool service was significantly faster and better than in other hotels. Kudos to them.

The service staff were mostly very friendly and helpful. Nothing to complain about! CRM is taken very seriously; it's very professional.

However, it didn't quite click for us because we've experienced all of this for half the price at other hotels.

I can't say why the hotel has to be so expensive. It's huge, lots of superficial ostentation, but there's no substance beneath the facade. The fancy "French" street with the Starbucks is a dark hall with overpriced, fake shops that are always empty.

Half the machines in the arcade are broken and probably over 10 years old. I played OutRun 2 as a kid...

The free visit to Land of Legends is great in theory. We took the earliest bus at 10:00 AM. Here, too, there are only enough loungers for guests of the hotel; everyone else is fighting for far too few loungers by the pools and slides.

At 10:20 AM, it was so crowded that the wait times for the slides were over 40 minutes. We only managed to use one slide. A complete waste of time. The wave pool feels much smaller in real life than it does in pictures and videos, and the waves aren't anything special... better to go to the sea.

Otherwise, it's absolutely overcrowded. The pools are smaller than at the hotel, and there are thousands of people...

We spent over €100 there on five non-alcoholic drinks. :-D

A taxi back costs €35 if you don't want to wait for the buses.

Yorum Metni:
We stayed at the hotel for a family vacation from June 28th to July 4th. We were thrilled to return to the hotel, which we had admired so much in the summer of 2015 before its renovations. Unfortunately, our excitement turned into disappointment.

Our check-in, originally scheduled for 2 PM, was only possible at 2:30 PM after much insistence and effort. Had we not insisted, we would have checked in even later.

Because all the aqua park and related attractions have been moved to Land of Legends, you need to use the shuttle service three times a day to access them (departures at 10:00 AM, 12:30 PM, and 7:00 PM; returns at 4:00 PM, 5:00 PM, and 10:00 PM). I think the shuttle times should be increased and adjusted. A small aqua park experience could have been left within the hotel. If you like aqua parks, this hotel doesn't have one. Planning a separate vacation to visit Land of Legends would be more cost-effective. Entry to Land of Legends is free, but you have to pay for food and drinks. Your all-inclusive concept is invalid here.

Tea service at breakfast or after dinner is problematic. Tea usually arrives 10 minutes after ordering, or you have to remind them if it doesn't arrive at all. We tried to get our own tea, but they wouldn't allow it.

The snack areas within the hotel are significantly weaker than before. The number of points and staff must be increased. Also, we loved their gözleme (Turkish flatbread) on our previous visit. The ladies who made gözleme during the day weren't there anymore, which was very disappointing.

I was bothered by the fact that some areas of the hotel were labeled "members only." I couldn't understand why such a practice exists in the same hotel, restaurant, or beach.

I was surprised that some staff didn't speak any Turkish. I wonder how we would have communicated if we didn't speak English. Also, I couldn't understand why a children's play in a Turkish hotel would only be performed in English. We've seen similar examples where it's managed in Turkish, English, Russian, or German.

There's not a single negative word to say about the sea. The sea in Belek is magnificent. The pools were also adequate and clean. Lifeguards and sports activities were also sufficient.
However, in the evenings, the sunbeds seemed to have been deliberately wet. We couldn't relax on them while listening to the sound of the waves. Why is that? :)

You need to make reservations at the à la carte restaurants. I had read reviews about problems, but we didn't experience any issues. Reservations opened at 10:00 AM, and we were able to make a reservation for 9:30 PM on the first day (Sunday) around 6:00 PM. The restaurant operations are very different from the hotel. We felt like we had arrived at a completely different place. “Akşam”, “Piazzetta Italiana”, “Z’Asya”, “Mykorini”. All were enjoyable and delicious restaurants.

In short, if I'm sure there have been improvements regarding our feedback, we would consider visiting again. However, I've listed this hotel as one I would never stay at for the same price under the same conditions.

Honestly, I don't understand why this hotel has so many positive reviews. After our stay, I simply can't comprehend the high overall rating.

I give it 2.5 out of 5 stars.

For the price, I had significantly higher expectations. Overall, the hotel was a disappointment.

The hotel was very crowded during our stay, which often made the service seem overwhelmed. The cleanliness of the room was particularly disappointing. We accidentally left a small toothpaste stain on the floor, which was still there four days later. This gave us the impression that the room hadn't been cleaned thoroughly.

Another major point of criticism was the bed. One side of the mattress was so soft and saggy that you practically sank into it. The other side, however, was perfectly fine. As a result, my wife and I had to alternate nights on the good side of the bed because a restful sleep was virtually impossible on the other side. We asked the hotel five consecutive days to either replace the mattress or find another solution. Unfortunately, no satisfactory solution was offered in response to our request.

During our vacation, I also became ill and asked the hotel to get me ibuprofen from a pharmacy. We were charged €70 for this. This price was completely unreasonable and I was very disappointed.

The food was generally good and of perfectly acceptable quality. The buffet restaurants were decent. However, the reservation system for the à la carte restaurants was disappointing. You had to log in every morning at 10:00 a.m. sharp to even have a chance of getting a table. Despite this, most restaurants were fully booked within a very short time. This regularly led to frustration. The only restaurant we were able to visit without any problems was People's, as no reservation was required there. We enjoyed this one.

Another point of criticism was the atmosphere at the pool and on the beach. Very loud music played there all day, so there were hardly any quiet areas to relax. According to the hotel description, we had expected a family hotel, but in reality, during the day it felt more like a party hotel. That was a real shame for us.

On a positive note, I'd like to highlight the arcade. The pinball machines, basketball hoops, and many other games were free to use – that was a really great idea and we enjoyed it a lot.

Overall, there are definitely some positive aspects. The food was good, and the free arcade was a real plus. However, for me, the price-performance ratio is completely off. Based on our experience, I wouldn't book this hotel again.
